_comment_tts_ref: Optional path to a 5-10s voice sample (.wav/.mp3) for zero-shot voice cloning. Leave empty to use Chatterbox' built-in default voice. Example: 'C:\\Users\\bezy\\Desktop\\voices\\meine_stimme.wav'.
_comment_tts_de_clone: Clone a voice for GERMAN too. When true, German uses Chatterbox Multilingual (same engine as English, ~3GB extra one-time download, voice cloning) instead of the fixed Piper voice. Needs a reference sample (tts_reference_audio_de, else tts_reference_audio). false = keep the offline Piper voice (faster, no VRAM, no cloning).
_comment_tts_ref_de: Optional GERMAN-specific 10-15s voice sample for cloning (used only when tts_de_clone is true). Empty = reuse tts_reference_audio. Use your own voice or a public-domain recording (e.g. LibriVox).
_comment_tts_exag: Emotion dial 0..1. 0 = flat/calm, 0.5 = neutral, 1 = dramatic. For shorts try 0.6-0.8.
_comment_tts_cfg: Guidance weight 0..1. Lower = more natural speech rhythm, higher = stricter text adherence. For energetic viral-narrator delivery try exaggeration 0.7 + cfg_weight 0.3.
_comment_tts_clone: Auto-clean the voice-clone reference (mono/trim-silence/~12s/normalize) before Chatterbox uses it. Leave true for any raw recording; set false only if your tts_reference_audio file is already perfectly prepared.
_comment_tts_lang: TTS language dispatcher. 'de' = Piper (offline German), 'en' = Chatterbox (offline English w/ voice cloning), 'auto' = heuristic on the script text.
_comment_tts_piper: Piper voice model name. Options: de_DE-thorsten-medium (default), de_DE-thorsten-high, de_DE-eva_k-x_low. Auto-downloaded on first use.
_comment_external_tts: Premium English TTS via F5-TTS in a SEPARATE venv (its torch/numpy/transformers clash with Chatterbox). 'off' = Chatterbox as before; 'f5' = clone your voice with F5-TTS (often more natural). Falls back to Chatterbox on any error. Setup: `python -m venv ..\f5tts-venv`, then in it `pip install torch torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128` and `pip install f5-tts`, then set external_tts_python below. Uses tts_reference_audio as the clone reference.
_comment_external_tts_python: Full path to the F5-TTS venv python.exe, e.g. 'C:\\Users\\bezy\\Desktop\\roblox-shorts\\f5tts-venv\\Scripts\\python.exe'. Empty = F5 disabled.
_comment_external_tts_ref_text: Optional transcript of your reference clip (what is actually said in tts_reference_audio). Empty = F5 auto-transcribes it (slightly slower first run).
_comment_voice_enhance: Denoise/enhance the voice in a SEPARATE venv. 'off' = none; 'resemble' = Resemble-Enhance (denoise + speech super-resolution, can subtly change timbre); 'deepfilter' = DeepFilterNet (denoise only, lighter). Applied to the TTS output; falls back to the raw voice on any error. Setup: own venv + `pip install resemble-enhance` (or `pip install deepfilternet`), then set voice_enhance_python.
_comment_voice_enhance_python: Full path to the enhance venv python.exe. Empty = voice enhance disabled.
_comment_gemini_moments: Set to 'gemini-2.5-pro' for noticeably better multi-clip moment picks at the cost of more free-tier quota per run. Defaults to gemini_model when empty.
_comment_video_encoder: Final video encode. 'auto' (recommended) uses NVENC on an NVIDIA GPU (5-10x faster than CPU on an RTX 3080) and falls back to x264 if NVENC isn't available. Force with 'nvenc' or 'cpu'. If NVENC ever produces a broken/blocky encode on your driver, set 'cpu'.
_comment_claude_cli: Use the locally installed `claude` CLI (your Claude subscription, no API key) for text tasks instead of Gemini — mainly multi-clip moment-picking. Opt-in, local/personal use only; slower than Gemini and counts against subscription limits. Falls back to Gemini on any failure. Can also be toggled per-run in the GUI.
_comment_claude_cli_model: Model passed to `claude --model` (e.g. 'sonnet', 'opus', 'haiku'). Empty = the CLI's current default. Sonnet/Opus are far better at moment-picking than Gemini Flash.
_comment_claude_cli_path: Path/name of the claude executable. Usually just 'claude' if it's on PATH.
_comment_grok_cli: Use the locally installed `grok` (Grok Build) CLI as the AI-image generator (your SuperGrok subscription, no API key). When on, it's tried FIRST in the AI-render path, with Cloudflare Flux / Pollinations as fallback. Opt-in, local/personal use only; slower than an API call (full agent spin-up, ~15s/image) and counts against subscription limits. Falls back automatically on any failure.
_comment_grok_cli_path: Path/name of the grok executable. Usually just 'grok' if it's on PATH (run `grok login` once first).
_comment_grok_cli_args: Optional extra CLI flags for the headless `grok -p` image call, space-separated (e.g. an auto-approve/non-interactive flag if your Grok Build version needs one to write files without a prompt). Empty = none.
_comment_higgsfield: Use the Higgsfield CLI to generate AI VIDEO for the video beats (your logged-in Higgsfield subscription, no API key). When on AND higgsfield_video_model is set, it's tried FIRST for video beats with Pexels stock as fallback. Needs '📹 Auch Stock-VIDEOS verwenden' enabled in the GUI. Opt-in: video gen is slow (~1-3 min/clip) and costs subscription credits.
_comment_higgsfield_model: The Higgsfield video job_set_type (model name). Find it by running a video job once in the terminal, then `higgsfield generate list` — copy the job_set_type. Empty = Higgsfield video disabled (falls back to Pexels). Image model for reference: nano_banana_2.
_comment_higgsfield_args: Optional extra flags appended to `higgsfield generate create <model> --prompt ... --wait --json`, space-separated (e.g. an aspect-ratio param like '--aspect_ratio 9:16' if your model supports it). Empty = none.
_comment_higgsfield_images: Use the Higgsfield CLI to generate the AI IMAGES (e.g. nano_banana_2) — great for the faceless stickman/doodle videos. When on, it's tried FIRST for every AI image beat, before Grok/Cloudflare/Pollinations. Your Higgsfield subscription, no API key. Falls back automatically on any failure.
_comment_higgsfield_image_model: The Higgsfield image model name (job_set_type). Default 'nano_banana_2' (the one you tested). Change if you want a different Higgsfield image model.
_comment_higgsfield_image_args: Optional extra flags for the image `generate create` call, space-separated. Empty = none.
_comment_image_style: AI-image look. 'auto' (recommended) = the planner picks the medium per beat: Roblox-render when the line is about a game character, photoreal/cinematic when it's about a real person, money, a city, an emotion, etc. — no more forced Roblox avatars on every image. Force one look for the whole video with 'roblox' (all Roblox), 'realistic' (no Roblox at all), or 'cinematic'; or put any custom style phrase here to append it to every prompt.
_comment_image_roblox_max: In 'auto' mode: the MAX number of AI images that may be actual Roblox 3D renders. Any beyond this are rewritten into real-world photoreal scenes (e.g. 'a lonely Roblox avatar' -> 'a lonely person'). Set 0 to never use Roblox in auto, raise it if you want more. Ignored when image_style forces a look. Default 2.
_comment_image_cooldown: Seconds to pause between AI image generations. 0 = off (default). If a long image run (many images) makes the PC hard-shutdown — that's a thermal/power protection trip, not a software crash — set this to 2-5 to let the GPU cool between renders. Also check GPU temps and PSU/power-cable seating; software can't power off a PC, only push marginal hardware over its limit.
_comment_emoji_font: Optional path to a color emoji font for caption emojis. Empty = auto-detect (Segoe UI Emoji on Windows, Noto Color Emoji on Linux). Example: 'C:\\Windows\\Fonts\\seguiemj.ttf'.
_comment_pixabay: Optional FREE Pixabay API key for reliable real-photo beats (30s signup, no credit card: https://pixabay.com/api/docs/). Empty = use the no-key sources Openverse/Wikimedia (less reliable on some networks). Can also be set via PIXABAY_API_KEY env.
_comment_yt_cookies_browser: Fixes YouTube '429 / Sign in to confirm you are not a bot'. Set to your browser: 'chrome', 'firefox', 'edge', or 'brave' — yt-dlp reads its logged-in YouTube cookies. Close that browser before running so the cookie DB isn't locked.
_comment_yt_cookies_file: Alternative to the browser option: path to a cookies.txt export (e.g. from the 'Get cookies.txt' browser extension). Wins over youtube_cookies_from_browser if both are set.
_comment_pexels: FREE Pexels API key for stock B-roll VIDEOS in the middle slot (https://www.pexels.com/api/ — 30s signup, no card). Enables the GUI's '📹 Auch Stock-VIDEOS verwenden' toggle. Empty = pipeline keeps using AI renders / photos only. Can also be set via PEXELS_API_KEY env.
_comment_use_whisperx: Opt-in WhisperX for word-level captions: force-aligns every word with a wav2vec2 model -> noticeably tighter karaoke timing (no drift). FREE, local, GPU. Falls back to plain faster-whisper automatically if it fails, so it never breaks a render. WhisperX 3.8+ has hard dependency conflicts with Chatterbox (torch ~2.8 / numpy 2 / transformers 4.x vs Chatterbox's torch cu124 / numpy<2 / transformers 5.2.0), so DON'T pip install it into the main .venv — set whisperx_python below to a SEPARATE venv instead.
_comment_whisperx_python: Path to a separate venv's python.exe that has whisperx installed (keeps the main venv's Chatterbox stack intact). Setup: `python -m venv ..\whisperx-venv` then in it `pip install torch torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128` and `pip install whisperx nvidia-cudnn-cu12 nvidia-cublas-cu12`. Then put the full path here, e.g. 'C:\\Users\\bezy\\Desktop\\roblox-shorts\\whisperx-venv\\Scripts\\python.exe'. Empty = use the main venv (only works if whisperx is somehow installed there).
_comment_download_max_height: Max resolution of the downloaded gameplay source. 1080 default. Set to 720 for MUCH faster downloads on long source videos — a vertical short is cropped+scaled anyway, so 720 looks identical there (only matters for full 16:9 long-videos).
_comment_telegram: Remote control via bot.py (text a job from your phone, get the finished mp4 back). Empty = disabled. Get a token from @BotFather. Run `python bot.py` on the PC (must stay awake).
_comment_telegram_chat: Your Telegram numeric chat id (message @userinfobot to get it). ONLY this id may trigger renders. 0 = disabled.
_comment_telegram_audio: Optional: dirs the bot uses for background music / SFX. With these set, bot shorts get a random music track + SFX automatically (like the GUI). e.g. 'C:\\Users\\bezy\\Desktop\\music'.
_comment_telegram_defaults: Your EXACT preferred short settings for bot renders — any GUI job key overrides the bot's built-in defaults. Example: {"caption_color": "#FFEB3B", "caption_font_size": 86, "voice_tempo": 1.0, "subscribe_sting_file": "C:\\Users\\bezy\\Desktop\\sfx\\sub.mp3", "music_track": "ein bisschen episch.mp3"}. Empty {} = just the built-in full-short defaults (all effects, emojis, karaoke, subscribe, music/sfx).
